## Sleep Duration and Quality Changes
- Over the past two weeks, daily sleep duration stayed between 240 and 300 minutes (4 to 5 hours), averaging only 268 minutes, indicating consistently insufficient sleep.
- Sleep quality scores ranged from 42 to 65 with an average of 54, which falls below the healthy sleep score threshold.
- No clear upward or downward trend was observed; both duration and quality fluctuated day-to-day without significant improvement or decline.
- Data were missing on March 22 and March 28, possibly due to device non-wear or recording issues.
- The longest sleep durations (300 minutes) and highest quality scores (65 and 63) occurred on March 21 and March 29, which may reflect weekend recovery sleep.

## Premature Ventricular Contraction (PVC) Changes
- PVC events were recorded on most days during the same two-week period. Whenever detected, they remained single isolated events (1 per day).
- Some days showed zero PVC events, and no data were available on March 22 and March 28, matching the missing sleep data days.
- The frequency and pattern of PVCs did not indicate any significant change over the two weeks; the burden remained consistently very low.

## Combined Assessment
- Both sleep metrics and PVC events remained relatively stable, with no notable worsening or improvement.
- The two days of missing data prevent a complete picture, but available data show persistent short/poor sleep alongside stable, infrequent PVCs.
